analysis:
Examined the visible changes in this batch: a new default-false ProviderLoopConfig.clusterMemberAnswersUpdateDrain flag (lines 40-43, 67, 85), two new path helpers in ClusterServiceAgent (lines 79-88), a doc-only comment change in ClusterMemberUpdateSlot (lines 17-20), the new ClusterPairUpdate.swift (pure decision logic, progress and request file I/O), and two new stored properties in ProviderLoop (clusterUpdateDrainID and clusterUpdateDrainTask). The ProviderLoop.swift head excerpt I was given (lines 1023-1294) shows only unchanged code, so the property additions were seen only in the file_changes patch.

No concrete security regression is identified. Defaults are conservative: the drain flag is off, and no new network surface, key handling, attestation, or authorization path is added in the visible code. The cluster-pair code does not touch the coordinator-provider trust boundary (TB-002) or the attestation and App Attest authorization path (TB-009, TB-011).

Open integration questions, because the files below were not supplied:
1. ClusterSupervisionFiles.read/write (used by readProgress, writeProgress, writeRequest and takeRequest) may not enforce owner-only permissions or no-follow semantics. The service-update-request.json and service-update.json files sit in the service directory; a same-UID process could forge a Request to trigger a restart or drain. That is arguably within the existing same-UID threat posture, as for T-059 and T-060. Also check that the takeRequest read-then-delete is not racy beyond a replay of a bounded-age request.
2. The partner progress is read over the pair link and is trusted as peer-reported. The pair link's authentication and the target-version binding are not visible. partnerState gives up or waits on a mismatched target, and a stale or unreachable partner maps to cannotCoordinate. Whether the caller proceeds alone safely (it says 'only when no pair runs') is not visible.
3. The ProviderLoop+ClusterUpdateDrain implementation was not supplied. It must be checked for drain admission, for what happens when the drained hold times out after 900 s and requests reopen, and for any bypass of the update/attestation gating.
4. Whether ClusterPairUpdateCycle verifies the release (signature and qualification) before staging and installing is not visible. The coordinated-update code should not widen T-043 or T-054.

No threat-model document update is needed from this batch alone.
